title: Robust Soft Skill Adaptation via Behavioral Localization in Tool-Using Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.30041v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Text skills can extend the capabilities of tool-using agents, but long skill descriptions increase computational costs. Soft prompts provide a compact alternative, yet learning from entire successful trajectories may also introduce unnecessary behavioral changes. We find that the useful effect of a text skill is highly concentrated in a small subset of trajectory positions. Based on this observation, we propose Behavioral Localization, which compares the frozen agent with and without the text skill to identify positions where the skill both increases the likelihood of successful tokens and meaningfully changes the next token distribution. We use these localized positions to supervise a short soft prompt. Experiments on SpreadsheetBench with a frozen Qwen3.6-35B-A3B agent show that the top 10\% of trajectory positions capture 96.12\% of the total positive skill gain. translated_title: 基于行为定位的工具使用智能体鲁棒软技能自适应
translated_abstract: 文本技能可以扩展工具使用智能体的能力，但冗长的技能描述会增加计算成本。软提示提供了一种紧凑的替代方案，然而从完整的成功轨迹中学习也可能引入不必要的行为改变。我们发现文本技能的有效作用高度集中在轨迹中一小部分位置上。基于这一观察，我们提出了行为定位方法，该方法通过比较冻结智能体在有和没有文本技能时的行为，来识别那些技能既能提高成功token可能性、又能显著改变下一个token分布的位置。我们使用这些定位出的位置来监督训练一个简短的软提示。在 SpreadsheetBench 上使用冻结的 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 智能体进行的实验表明，轨迹位置中前10%的部分捕获了总技能正向增益的96.12%。在共享提示设置中，选择性监督将成功率提升（原文此处截断）。
tldr: 提出行为定位方法，通过找出轨迹中技能真正发挥作用的关键位置来监督训练短软提示，使冻结的工具使用智能体能以极低成本获得文本技能的绝大部分增益并避免不必要的行为改变。
en_tdlr: Proposes Behavioral Localization, which identifies the small subset of trajectory positions where a text skill is truly effective and uses them to supervise a compact soft prompt, capturing 96.12% of the skill's positive gain with only the top 10% of positions while avoiding unnecessary behavioral changes.
